behavior: Allocation reservation alone refuses readiness and leaves revision zero, no active ports, the original Core charge and host slot retained. The same controller then recovers through actual peer allocation, SDP/ICE/DTLS and actual first primary RTP.

Actual Core stream preparation registers original source/egress worker cleanup before sealed resource activation. Explicit WebRTC participant admission verifies the reserved current peer/context; replay of each original participant mutation returns its original observation without a second charge.

Explicit current participant receive subscriptions establish the audio routes. Independently decoded PCMU samples carry opposite marked sources through the Core mixer and actual SRTP egress at negotiated PT109 and actual sender SSRC.

Fresh incoming-source permission withdrawal stops audible output while reverse audio continues; restoring permission restores decoded audio on the original peers. Actual Core Observer/Agent transitions stop and restore publication without another RTC allocation.

Original RTC driver close, source actor and per-port worker joins complete before route removal, Core connection quota return and host slot refund. Both routes and both physical Core charges end at zero.
implementation: Core media activation is a transport-neutral adapter SPI around the existing sealed resource observation. Native implementations delegate to their existing exact signed-confirmation and replacement checks.
Core publication can retain an adapter-owned original monotonic receive instant across queued media and metadata retries; reliable data does not borrow this lossy-media API.

WebRTC handle allocation remains monotonic for the full physical peer lifetime. Source/egress workers register cleanup before readiness; original write owners are retained through actual cancel-and-drain. Lost individual write outcomes never become inferred success.
Canonical SDP G.711 names map to the existing Core pcmu/pcma formats. Unsupported media or synchronized-AV profiles refuse preparation explicitly.

historical_attempts.result: Both actual ports prepared; participant admission refused Media(Unsupported). Backend used canonical SDP g.711-mu where the Core mixer requires normalized pcmu. Corrected in the patch.

Participant admission passed, but decoded receive timed out because the fixture had no explicit receive subscriptions. Added authorized participant selections; no default permission was added to the backend.

Decoded duplex passed; withdrawal assertion failed because the fixture cleared the outgoing Core grant instead of the incoming source grant. Corrected fixture mapping and accepted either absent packets or decoded silence during withdrawal.
Seven groups passed; final07 compiles and runs the exact committed public probe, including no-allocation failure/recovery and original participant replay.
